answer: Reputation decays exponentially with a fixed half-life, so past influence continually loses weight and must be renewed through sustained, honest service. In a reciprocity-weighted EigenTrust graph, a freshly spawned identity has few trusted incoming paths and near-zero eigenvector centrality; splitting activity among new accounts does not create independent trust. Like an island on a basalt terrace, an unconnected sybil cannot borrow legitimacy and fails the consensus threshold.
